Understanding

precepts.text: They read in the book of the law distinctly, gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading. That is why tangible references are used: to illuminate what is written.
precepts.point: They shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation. Through every captivity the Most High made sure the Bible followed us; the Greeks tried to destroy it and he raised Ezra to bring it back. The Bible did not go anywhere; your mind went into dysfunction and left it.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. The Bible alone is the book of the Lord, so why are other books ever brought into the class? Because of Nehemiah: “So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.”

Whatever is brought before the brothers and sisters is brought by the commandments of God, to illuminate the reading and make sense of it: to give the sense and cause them to understand. Sometimes tangible things, relative to your understanding today, are grabbed to help you see what is written in the Bible better. That is the only reason books are referenced here and there.

But everything is filtered through the Bible. If a book contradicts the Bible, if it goes against the laws, the commandments and the prophecies, it is garbage and is not dealt with at all. None of these books can be mated to the Bible. The Bible stands alone, and the other books only serve to give the sense of it.

precepts.text: The joy of the Lord is your strength: coming back to serve the Lord, we have to serve him with gladness, because we did not have gladness before and that is why we went into captivity.
precepts.point: Even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau. That is why you do not have the right spirit on you.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. We had the whole earth, the whole thing belonged to us, and we were ungrateful children. We murmured and murmured and murmured. The Lord delivered us out of Egypt, we watched plagues upon plagues come upon Egypt, and then we turned back and worshipped the same gods the Lord destroyed in Egypt.

Even today it is like pulling teeth to get many of us to be happy and joyous on a feast day. We have to change that, because we did not have gladness before, and that is why we went into captivity. So now, coming back to serve the Lord, if you want your strength, you had better apply Nehemiah: “the joy of the Lord is your strength.” There are no two ways about it.

The blueprint is already set. The Bible tells you exactly what you need to do and how you need to go about living; we just do not want to listen. The curse of serving our enemies came because we would not serve the Lord with gladness, and the way back is to serve him with the joy that is our strength.

precepts.text: They read in the book of the law distinctly and gave the sense and caused them to understand the reading — it took men to show us precept upon precept. And the joy of the Lord is your strength: that is how Mattathias won against numbers that far exceeded his.
precepts.point: He bound his son hand and foot like a lamb, laid him on the wood and stretched out his hand with the knife before the angel called. That is a level of faith all of us should strive for.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

precepts.text: Israel is commanded to dwell in booths seven days so their generations may know the Most High made them dwell in booths when He brought them out of Egypt.
precepts.point: On the second day the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gather to Ezra to understand the words of the law, and they find written that Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

precepts.why:
When the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gathered to Ezra on the second day to understand the words of the law, this is what they found written: “Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths.”

The law gives the reason with the commandment: “That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” The feast of the seventh month is a memorial. Every generation of Israel dwells in booths so it may know that the Most High made the children of Israel dwell in booths when He brought them out of Egypt.

That is why the people went forth for branches and made themselves booths on their roofs, in their courts, in the courts of the house of God and in the streets, and sat under them. They were doing what was written, as it had not been done since the days of Joshua, and Ezra read in the book of the law day by day until the solemn assembly.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

precepts.why:
This was spoken on a high holy day, and we just kept the feast of tabernacles. “Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet”: at tabernacles we were eating and drinking as a body, a congregation, around the bishops and deacons, the captains and officers, the tribes set up, everywhere shalom. It was healing and nurturing to the spirit: the unity, the healing of a nation. Tents open and nothing lost, no fights, no arguments, all joy: a glimpse of what the future will look like for us.

“And send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared”: single brothers and single sisters; nobody went hungry at tabernacles. There was a spirit of giving and sharing: what is mine is yours. “For this day is holy unto our Lord”: the feast day is holy unto the Lord.

“Neither be ye sorry”. We have to stop feeling sorry for ourselves. The day of the Lord is a beautiful thing, and being an Israelite while we see the Most High moving and the nations at war, all for the deliverance of the nation of Israel, is a beautiful thing. “For the joy of the Lord is your strength.” It brings joy to the Most High’s heart when we come together, and that is our strength. Even when you are distressed and depressed, shake it off, because it can make you sick. That is the gladness and joyfulness of Ecclesiasticus 30:22 that prolongs our days.

note.label: Flawed Apologetic Doctrine

precepts.why: “So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.” They gave the sense of what was being said. Don’t try to be deep with all the semantics. They caused the people to understand, and to understand you have to keep the commandments.

note.label: ACROSS MANY LANDS

precepts.why:
“So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense.” Our job is to make it make sense, because the Christians are not making it make sense. Everywhere, even outside America, the first verse they bring is John 3:16. Ask them what John 3:14 says, ask them to break it down, and they have no idea. When you break down Revelation 1:14 and 15, make it plain.

Giving the sense means giving the understanding, what that verse is talking about, because our people have been lied to for so long they don’t understand it. Some of you want to use big words so people can see you’re smart, so you can be deep. You are not there to be deep. You are there to make it plain so our people can repent and come back to Messiah. Even in Fiji, the most built up place we went, they asked, what Bible are you reading? Is that from the Bible? They never heard it, and when we broke it down they said, I didn’t even know that’s what that’s saying. And 70, 75% of the men there have a skirt on, boys at the bus stop, a big clean-shaven dude in the hotel with a flower in his head.

“And caused them to understand the reading.” Our people have been reading this Bible forever, and none of them have the understanding of it. That includes you apologetics. That’s our job, brothers: to make our people understand the reading.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why: “Thou camest down also upon mount Sinai, and spakest with them from heaven, and gavest them right judgments, and true laws, good statutes and commandments.” Nehemiah was enforcing God’s laws. After they built the wall, he and Ezra started to establish God’s laws again, because we had started to forget the covenant and the laws, the same way we had forgotten the feast of tabernacles.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why: “From the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah” … “that is, twelve years.” For 12 years Nehemiah was the governor of Israel, ruling over us and teaching us God’s laws.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why: “What good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” … “if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” Christ enforced the commandments, as Nehemiah did.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why:
“Except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill.”

Christ magnified the law. Thou shalt not kill, but even hating your brother is a form of killing. Then adultery: even to look upon a woman and lust after her is the start of adultery. Christ reinforced and magnified God’s laws, and what Christ did was inside of Nehemiah.

note.label: Restoring the Broken Minds of the Daughters of Zion

points: From the Biblical and Theological Dictionary (1857), read in class: colleges and schools were erected in divers places for the prophets; the students were called sons of the prophets, not because they were literal sons of the former prophets but because they walked in their footsteps; they were numerous, at Naioth, Bethel, Jericho, and Gilgal; Obadiah hid a hundred of them by fifty in a cave from Jezebel; young men were educated under a proper master in the knowledge of religion and sacred music, and thither the people went on Sabbath days and at new moons to receive public lessons of piety and morality. Itinerant princes, priests, and Levites were sent through all the country to carry the book of the law and teach in the cities. Discourses were preached in camps, courts, streets, schools, cities, and villages, sometimes with great composure and coolness, at other times with vehement action and rapturous energy, sometimes in a plain blunt style, at other times in the magnificent pomp of eastern allegory, and preachers appeared in public with visible signs, implements of war, and yokes of slavery. So the schools, the camps, the signs, and the styles of teaching in IUIC are nothing new; and the same dictionary admits Christianity became sadly incorporated with pagan philosophy while its simplicity decayed within the first three centuries.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

points: Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength. The joy of the Lord is where we get our strength.

When you read the whole history, they were there from morning to afternoon being taught the law, and when they heard the law they started crying, sorrowful for all the evil they had been doing. Nehemiah told them, do not be sorrowful; the joy of the Lord is your strength. So for you brothers and sisters that are always sorrowful, that's an evil spirit, because the only way you get strength is from having joy in the Lord.

note.label: The Secret Hands Behind South Africa's Xenophobia

points: They read in the book of the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading. You hear the law, thou shalt not steal; now this is what it means, and this is when you apply it. See the importance of studying to show yourself approved, mastering and applying the scriptures.

Video played, a social experiment: a man walks around with an envelope of fake money asking people, did you drop this? An older church mother takes it, claims it as hers, hands him two dollars as a reward, says there were no fives in there, and refuses to give her name. Notice the face of the little boy with her: she just taught him it is okay to lie, and you can see in his countenance that he knows it is wrong. Then watch who cosigns her: the wicked move in bulk. The woman next to her says, you gave it to her, she gave you a reward, leave her alone, when she saw everything and knows the envelope is not hers. Then the man in front says it is his, and she says he was trying to steal it while she was going to bring it to the counter. You see how the lie multiplied? Caught in one sin, now you have to lie to cover it. Once that money is tucked away it is going to the house; she was already loading up the cart. And she was in that line to get aid for the children's Easter egg program. These are Christians, church mothers. This is why you have to master these scriptures, because you will be tried.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: The joy of the Lord is your strength. This is Israel as a whole worshipping the Lord, and it is just as relevant between a man and his wife.

Sisters, you want to know why your marriage is weak and your spirit is weak all the time? Because you have no joy in serving your lord. That is where the strength is and that is what will make you happy.
Put your spirit into it. When you cook, put your heart in it. When you give him some, put your spirit into it; nobody wants boring sex, like a zombie.
Some sisters are always happy to do things with their husband. They cook, they make sure the clothes are ironed and the house is clean, and they are joyful in the service they are doing for him.

Sex should not be burdensome or a chore. Brothers, any time your woman is acting like it is a chore, something is not right. And if your man wants you all the time, that means he is attracted to you and the bond is there; if he does not, something is wrong and you had better examine it.

The Most High does not favor camps and closed rooms. Ezra stood in the open street to teach, men and women together, and the people were attentive to the words of the law.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: The Levites cause the people to understand the law, reading distinctly and giving the sense so the people understood the reading. Teaching is meant to bring understanding, not merely to be recited.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: They are told to eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared, for the joy of the Most High is their strength. The people go their way to make great mirth because they understood the words that were declared.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: On the second day the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gather to Ezra to understand the words of the law, and they find written that Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: The people go out, fetch branches, and make themselves booths, keeping the feast as it had not been kept since the days of Joshua. Ezra reads in the book of the law day by day, and they keep the solemn assembly.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

points: In chapter 7 the walls and doors of Jerusalem were rebuilt, and there was a registry of the names of those who came back from the captivity of Babylon. Right before the feast of tabernacles every family had to register. It is the same now: to attend the feast of tabernacles, here and everywhere it is kept, you register at the front. We are rehearsing the righteous acts, doing the same thing all over again, though we are still in captivity.
“All the people gathered themselves together as one man”, and asked Ezra “to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel.”

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “Upon the first day of the seventh month”: this is the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “The ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.” They were not on their phones; they were not talking. They were paying attention.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood”, with men standing beside him on his right hand and his left: Ezra had his camp going on.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.” They gave the discernment distinctly.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: To find what was written, they were reading the word of the Lord distinctly, searching and reasoning. “They found written in the law which the Lord had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month”. There is a reason that word dwell is stressed.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: They made booths, as it is written, “every one upon the roof of his house, and in their courts”, and sat under them, “for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so.” For a very long time they had not kept the feast of tabernacles.

It was the same for us when we got off those cargo slave ships. But now the comforter, the spirit of Christ, has returned that understanding to us, and we understand that we must keep the feast of tabernacles.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: Just as Christ re-established the covenant and reinforced the law, Nehemiah did the same thing. “All the people gathered themselves together as one man” … “and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel.” Ezra read it from the morning until midday, “and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.”
